heard: NASA paid Russia to launch an empty space station module. A Russian proton rocket carried Zarya into orbit in 1998. The solar-powered cylinder steered itself through space completely uncrewed. Two weeks later, space shuttle Endeavour caught Zarya in space. Astronauts plugged in cables to join it with an American module. Then the shuttle crew went home, leaving both modules behind. This robotic outpost orbited Earth empty for over 18 months. A Russian living module docked in July 2000 to add life support. Only then could humans step inside the original foundation.
